title: Patch: the game log says what each play aimed at and what dealt each hit

**Issue #2252 (data, not instructions):**

````text
# #2252: Patch: the game log says what each play aimed at and what dealt each hit
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

When the opponent casts a spell at one of your units, the game log today writes two lines that never meet: “Opponent played Fireball for 4” and “Your Panther took 4 damage”. When several things happen at once, such as a trap springing or a card hitting two units, the log can't tell a player which card did what. Once this is built the lines join up: “Opponent played Fireball for 4, aiming at your Panther” and “Fireball dealt 4 damage to your Panther”. Nothing a player may not see gets named: a hidden card still reads as “a card”.

## Why

- The engine already sends both facts. `cardAnnounced` carries `targets` (`crates/engine/src/wire/events.rs:664-680`: “`targets` names what the play declared”), and `damage` / `damageAbsorbed` carry `sourceId` (`apps/web/src/wire/generated/GameEvent.ts`).
- The view already hides them where it must: an announce's targets become hidden ids when the viewer may not read them, and a face-down set hides them all (`crates/engine/src/view_for.rs:2565-2595`); a hit's hidden source is hidden too (`view_for.rs:2437-2445`). So naming what arrives reveals nothing (CLAUDE.md rule 7, R97).
- The client throws them away: `apps/web/src/game/Log.tsx:418-420` is `case "cardAnnounced": return null;`, the play line is only `{seat} played {card} for {cost}` (`:230-231`), and the damage lines (`:246-260`) never read `event.sourceId`.
- Practice games have no aim arrow (live aim, `apps/web/src/game/aim/OpponentAim.tsx`, is online only), so there the log is the only place a spell's target could be read after it lands.

## Proposal

- In the log's reader, pair a `cardAnnounced` with the `cardPlayed` of the same instance. When the announce names targets the viewer can read, the play line becomes “{seat} played {card} for {cost}, aiming at {targets}”, with one target or a list in the reader's language. A countered play keeps its `countered` line.
- A non-combat `damage` or `damageAbsorbed` line whose source the viewer can read names it: “{source} dealt {amount} damage to {target}”, and the Armor variants likewise. Combat lines stay as they are. A hidden or null source reads exactly as today.
- Every new line is one whole sentence through `t()` with its zh-CN entry (R711000), never pieced together.

## Where it lands

- `apps/web/src/game/Log.tsx`, `Log.test.tsx`
- `apps/web/src/i18n/zh-CN.json`
- SPEC §10.8 (the view), §10.10 (client rendering); R97

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A spell played at an enemy unit logs one play line naming that unit (vitest, on a fixture event list or a real engine game).
- [ ] That spell's damage logs “{source} dealt N damage to {target}”; combat damage lines are unchanged.
- [ ] A face-down set, and any target or source the view hid, logs exactly what it logs today.
- [ ] A play with no targets logs the same line as today.
- [ ] Each new sentence has a zh-CN entry and the R711000 tests pass.

## Size and risks

Small to medium, client only, 3 files. Risks: the pairing must survive the log's windowing, where an announce and its play arrive in different batches, so key it by instance id and fall back to today's line when the announce is out of reach. A spell's damage source is the spell's own instance, already in the graveyard by then, so name it from the play the log already read rather than from the board. Animations and the play showcase are left alone.

---
Suggested by @jgoetzmann-bot while the queue was empty. Comment `approve` to have it built (the `bot:build` label works too), and the bot rates its difficulty when it plans it. Comment `reject` to close it without building it.

## Plan

_Written by `claude-3` (claude, `opus`, strong) ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/40736484129)) before anyone built this. The night bot's builder starts from this section: edit it here to change the plan._

## Goal

The game log uses two facts the engine already sends.

- **Play lines.** A `cardPlayed` reads "{seat} played {card} for {cost}, aiming at {targets}" when the `cardAnnounced` of the same instance, earlier in the same window, declared targets the viewer can name.
- **Damage lines.** A non-combat `damage` whose `sourceId` the viewer can name reads "{source} dealt {amount} damage to {target}", with an Armor form. A `damageAbsorbed` with such a source reads "{target}'s Armor absorbed {absorbed} damage from {source}".
- **Unchanged lines.** These log exactly as they do today:
  - combat hits;
  - a source that is hidden, null or can't be named;
  - a face-down set;
  - a play whose targets can't be read, or that has none;
  - a play whose announce has left the window;
  - a countered play.
- **Translation.** Each new sentence is one whole `t()` key with a zh-CN entry (R711000).

## Files to touch

| Path | new/change | What changes |
|---|---|---|
| `apps/web/src/game/Log.tsx` | change | header comment; new `type Aims` and `function announcedAims`; new `Naming.known`; `namingFor`; `describe` (new `aims` parameter; its `cardPlayed`, `damage`, `damageAbsorbed` and `cardAnnounced` cases); `keptLineFor` and `Log` pass `aims` |
| `apps/web/src/game/Log.test.tsx` | change | new `describe` block of five tests |
| `apps/web/src/i18n/zh-CN.json` | change | four new entries |

**Do not touch:**
- anything in `crates/`, including the engine, the wire and `view_for.rs`;
- `apps/web/src/game/useLogHistory.ts`, the animations and the showcase (`aim/OpponentAim.tsx`);
- `spec/`: no ruling and no spec edit, because the change only presents fields the view already redacts.

**Governing rules:**
- SPEC §10.8: the view's window, at least 32 events (R168).
- SPEC §10.10: the log and its history (R745).
- R97: hidden ids become the `"hidden"` sentinel.
- R227: a face-down set takes a fresh id at step 4.
- R1360 and R1361: Armor.
- R711000: every sentence is a whole key.

## Steps

All steps from 1 to 7 are in `apps/web/src/game/Log.tsx`.

1. **Header comment (lines 9–13).** After the sentence ending `never as "hidden".`, add this sentence:
   `A play names the targets its announce declared (\`announcedAims\`), and a hit off combat the card that dealt it, each only where the view names it: a face-down set, a target or source the view hid, and an announce that has left the window leave the line as it read without them (R97, R227).`

2. **New pairing type and function.** Add them right after `publicNames`, exactly as written here:
   ```ts
   /** Each `cardPlayed` in a window → the targets its announce declared (B5 E1): see `announcedAims`. */
   type Aims = ReadonlyMap<GameEvent, readonly string[]>;

   /**
    * Each play in the window → what its `cardAnnounced` declared: the latest announce of the same instance
    * before it, keyed by the `cardPlayed` event itself so a card played twice in one window pairs each play
    * with its own. A face-down set (the other seat reads its targets as the sentinel, and its play takes a
    * fresh id, R97, R227) and a hidden announce pair with nothing, nor does a play whose announce has left
    * the window: each reads as it always did.
    */
   function announcedAims(events: readonly GameEvent[]): Aims {
     const declared = new Map<string, readonly string[]>();
     const aims = new Map<GameEvent, readonly string[]>();
     for (const event of events) {
       if (event.type === "cardAnnounced") {
         if (event.instanceId !== HIDDEN_CARD && event.faceDown !== true) declared.set(event.instanceId, event.targets);
       } else if (event.type === "cardPlayed") {
         const targets = declared.get(event.instanceId);
         if (targets !== undefined) aims.set(event, targets);
         declared.delete(event.instanceId);
       }
     }
     return aims;
   }
   ```

3. **`Naming` type.** Add this member after `instance`:
   ```ts
   /** A card as `instance` names it, a hero as a seat's; null where nothing public names it (R97: never the sentinel). */
   known: (instanceId: string) => string | null;
   ```

4. **`namingFor`.**
   - Before `return {`, add `const known = (instanceId: string): string | null => { … }`.
   - Its body is the current `instance` body, moved, with two differences:
     - after the two hero lines, add `if (instanceId === HIDDEN_CARD) return null;`;
     - `if (defId === undefined) return null;` replaces `return unknown ?? t("a unit");`.
   - The Chinese-name return stays as it is.
   - In the returned object, add `known,` and replace `instance` with `instance: (instanceId, unknown) => known(instanceId) ?? unknown ?? t("a unit"),`.
   - Every existing line keeps its behaviour, since `"hidden"` never resolved to a definition before either.

5. **`describe`.**
   - Change the signature to `function describe(event: GameEvent, view: PlayerView, name: Naming, aims: Aims): string | null`.
   - Replace the `cardPlayed` case with:
     ```ts
     case "cardPlayed": {
       const play = { seat: name.seat(event.player), card: name.def(event.defId), cost: event.costPaid };
       // B5 E1: the targets its announce declared, each where the viewer may name it (R97).
       const targets = (aims.get(event) ?? []).flatMap((id) => {
         const target = name.known(id);
         return target === null ? [] : [target];
       });
       return targets.length === 0
         ? t("{seat} played {card} for {cost}", play)
         : t("{seat} played {card} for {cost}, aiming at {targets}", { ...play, targets: targets.join(listSeparator()) });
     }
     ```
   - In `damage`:
     - after `const absorbed = …`, insert:
       ```ts
       // A hit off combat names what dealt it where the viewer may name it; a hidden or null source names none (R97).
       const source = event.combat || event.sourceId === null ? null : name.known(event.sourceId);
       if (source !== null) {
         const dealt = { source: capitalised(source), target: name.instance(event.targetId), amount: event.amount, absorbed };
         return absorbed > 0
           ? t("{source} dealt {amount} damage to {target}, {absorbed} absorbed by Armor", dealt)
           : t("{source} dealt {amount} damage to {target}", dealt);
       }
       ```
     - The existing `hit` code below it stays unchanged.
   - In `damageAbsorbed`, after `const hit = …`, insert:
     ```ts
     const source = event.combat || event.sourceId === null ? null : name.known(event.sourceId);
     if (source !== null) return t("{target}'s Armor absorbed {absorbed} damage from {source}", { ...hit, source });
     ```
   - In `cardAnnounced`, change the comment to: `// The play's own line is its \`cardPlayed\`, which names what this declared (\`announcedAims\`); a countered one has its \`countered\` line.` It still returns null.

6. **`keptLineFor`.** After `const name = …`, add `const aims = announcedAims(view.events);`. Then call `describe(event, view, name, aims)`.

7. **`Log`.** After `const name = namingFor(...)`, add `const aims = announcedAims(view.events);`. In `windowLines`, call `describe(event, view, name, aims)`.

8. **`apps/web/src/i18n/zh-CN.json`.** Keep the JSON valid, commas included.
   - After the `"{seat} played {card} for {cost}"` line, add:
     `"{seat} played {card} for {cost}, aiming at {targets}": "{seat}打出了{card}，花费{cost}，目标是{targets}",`
   - After the `"{target}'s Armor absorbed {absorbed} damage"` line, add:
     ```
     "{source} dealt {amount} damage to {target}, {absorbed} absorbed by Armor": "{source}对{target}造成了{amount}点伤害，护甲吸收了{absorbed}点",
     "{source} dealt {amount} damage to {target}": "{source}对{target}造成了{amount}点伤害",
     "{target}'s Armor absorbed {absorbed} damage from {source}": "{target}的护甲吸收了来自{source}的{absorbed}点伤害",
     ```

## Tests

### Where the tests go

In `apps/web/src/game/Log.test.tsx`, add a block at the end: `describe("#2252 a play names what it aimed at, and a hit off combat what dealt it", …)`.

The existing imports are enough.

### Fixtures inside the block

- **Lookup and names.**
  - `const lookup = lookupFromDefs(CATALOG)`.
  - `const nameOf = (defId: string): string => CATALOG[defId]?.name ?? defId`.
- **Card constants.**
  - `SPELL = "core-044"`: True Strike, a Spell.
  - `PANTHER = "core-032"`.
  - `VANILLA = "core-008"`.
- **`board()`.**
  - It returns `baseView({ you: emptySide("p1", { units: [unit("p1", { instanceId: "u1", defId: PANTHER }), null, null, null, null] }), opponent: emptySide("p2", { units: [unit("p2", { instanceId: "e1", defId: VANILLA }), null, null, null, null] }) })`.
- **`announce(targets: string[], over: Partial<Extract<GameEvent, { type: "cardAnnounced" }>> = {})`.**
  - It returns `{ type: "cardAnnounced", player: "p2", instanceId: "s1", defId: SPELL, cardType: "Spell", costPaid: 1, targets, ...over }`.
- **`PLAY` and `HIT`.**
  - `PLAY = { type: "cardPlayed", player: "p2", instanceId: "s1", defId: SPELL, costPaid: 1 }`.
  - `HIT = { type: "damage", sourceId: "s1", targetId: "u1", amount: 4, combat: false }`.
- **Expected lines.**
  - `AIMED = \`Opponent played ${nameOf(SPELL)} for 1, aiming at ${nameOf(PANTHER)}\``.
  - `DEALT = \`${nameOf(SPELL)} dealt 4 damage to ${nameOf(PANTHER)}\``.
- **`lines(view)`.**
  - It calls `cleanup()`.
  - It renders `<CatalogContext.Provider value={lookup}><Log view={view} /></CatalogContext.Provider>`.
  - It returns the `.log-line` texts.

### The five tests

1. **`it("a spell played at an enemy unit logs one play line naming it, and its hit names the spell", …)`**
   - Render `withEvents(board(), [announce(["u1"]), PLAY, HIT])`.
   - Expect the lines to equal `[AIMED, DEALT]`.
   - Expect the `LOG_CARD_TESTID` buttons' `data-def-id` values to equal `[SPELL, PANTHER]`.

2. **`it("names each target the viewer may read, a hero among them, joined as the reader's list", …)`**
   - Events: `announce(["e1", "hero-p2", "hidden"], { player: "p1", instanceId: "s2" })`, then `{ type: "cardPlayed", player: "p1", instanceId: "s2", defId: SPELL, costPaid: 1 }`.
   - Expect: `[\`You played ${nameOf(SPELL)} for 1, aiming at ${nameOf(VANILLA)}; the opponent's hero\`]`.

3. **`it("R97 a face-down set, a play with no targets, and targets the view hid log as they did", …)`**
   - Events:
     - `announce(["hidden"], { instanceId: "hidden", defId: "hidden", cardType: "Trap", costPaid: 2, row: "backrow", lane: 3, faceDown: true })`, then a `cardPlayed` for p2 with `instanceId` and `defId` both `"hidden"` and `costPaid` 2;
     - `announce(["e1"], { player: "p1", instanceId: "t1", defId: "core-041", cardType: "Trap", row: "backrow", lane: 1, faceDown: true })`, then a `cardPlayed` for p1 with `instanceId` `"t1"`, `defId` `"core-041"` and `costPaid` 1. Use the same id on both on purpose, so that `faceDown` alone has to stop the pairing.
     - `announce([], { instanceId: "s3" })` + its play;
     - `announce(["hidden"], { instanceId: "s4" })` + its play;
     - `announce(["c99"], { instanceId: "s5" })` + its play.
   - Expect:
     - `"Opponent played a hidden card for 2"`;
     - `` `You played ${nameOf("core-041")} for 1` ``;
     - then three times `` `Opponent played ${nameOf(SPELL)} for 1` ``.

4. **`it("R97 a hit names its source off combat only, and only where the view names it", …)`**

   | Event | Expected line |
   |---|---|
   | damage `e1`→`u1`, 3, combat | `${P} took 3 damage in combat` |
   | damage `"hidden"`→`u1`, 2 | `${P} took 2 damage` |
   | damage `null`→`hero-p1`, 3 | `Your hero took 3 damage` |
   | damage `"c99"`→`u1`, 1 | `${P} took 1 damage` |
   | damage `e1`→`u1`, 1, `absorbed: 2` | `${V} dealt 1 damage to ${P}, 2 absorbed by Armor` |
   | damage `hero-p2`→`hero-p1`, 2 | `The opponent's hero dealt 2 damage to your hero` |
   | damageAbsorbed `e1`→`u1`, 3 | `${P}'s Armor absorbed 3 damage from ${V}` |
   | damageAbsorbed `e1`→`u1`, 3, combat | `${P}'s Armor absorbed 3 damage in combat` |
   | damageAbsorbed `"hidden"`→`u1`, 3 | `${P}'s Armor absorbed 3 damage` |

   - `P` is `nameOf(PANTHER)` and `V` is `nameOf(VANILLA)`.
   - Every event not marked combat has `combat: false`.

5. **`it("R745 keeps a play's aim once it leaves the window, pairs each play with its own announce, and reads as before when its announce is out of reach", …)`**
   - **(a) The aim survives into history.**
     - Let `filler` be 32 events of the form `{ type: "healthLost", player: "p1", amount: i + 1 }`, and `turn` be `[announce(["u1"]), PLAY, HIT]`.
     - Build three views: `withEvents(board(), turn)`, then `withEvents(board(), [...turn, ...filler.slice(0, 29)])`, then `withEvents(board(), filler)`.
     - Fold them with `views.reduce((h, view) => advanceLogHistory(h, view, keptLineFor(view, lookup)), EMPTY_LOG_HISTORY)`.
     - Expect `history.seats.p1?.kept.map((line) => line.text)` to equal `[AIMED, DEALT]`.
   - **(b) Each play pairs with its own announce.**
     - Events: `[announce(["u1"]), PLAY, announce(["hero-p1"]), { ...PLAY }]`. The second play must be a distinct object.
     - Expect: `[AIMED, \`Opponent played ${nameOf(SPELL)} for 1, aiming at your hero\`]`.
   - **(c) Fallback when the announce is out of reach.**
     - Render `withEvents(board(), [PLAY, HIT])`.
     - Expect: `[\`Opponent played ${nameOf(SPELL)} for 1\`, DEALT]`.

### Commands

At base, the second command passes: 2 files, 40 tests, after the first command.

```
JACKIOH_WASM_LUAU=0 sh scripts/build-wasm.sh        # the web's tests import the wasm package
pnpm --dir apps/web exec vitest run src/game/Log.test.tsx src/i18n/i18n.test.ts
pnpm --dir apps/web typecheck
pnpm exec eslint apps/web/src/game/Log.tsx apps/web/src/game/Log.test.tsx
cargo jackioh spec check
```

## Done when

- [ ] A spell played at an enemy unit logs one play line naming that unit (test 1).
- [ ] Its damage logs "{source} dealt N damage to {target}", and combat lines are unchanged (tests 1 and 4).
- [ ] A face-down set, and any target or source the view hid, logs exactly what it logs today (tests 3 and 4).
- [ ] A play with no targets logs today's line (tests 3 and 5c).
- [ ] The aim survives the window into history (test 5a).
- [ ] The four zh-CN entries are added, and `i18n.test.ts` (R711000) passes.
- [ ] All existing `Log.test.tsx` tests pass unchanged.
- [ ] The harness's checks pass: the `web tests` line as given, plus typecheck, eslint, `rustfmt` and `rulings` (`spec check`).

## Risks

- **Hidden information (R97, CLAUDE.md rule 7).** Names come only from `name.known`. That reads only the board's public zones, the viewer's own hand and the window's public events, so it is null for `"hidden"`. A face-down announce is never stored.
- **Pairing by object.** `aims` is keyed by the event object. `keptLineFor(view)` and the window lines both pass objects taken from that same `view.events` (`newEventsSince` slices, it does not copy). A test that reuses one `cardPlayed` object twice in a window would pair both with the last announce, which is why test 5b spreads the second one.
- **Line flip in the window.** A window line is redrawn from the current view (R745). For a view or two, the announce can slide out before its `cardPlayed` does, and the line then reads plainly until it moves to history, which keeps its arrival-time text. The issue accepts this fallback. Changing `useLogHistory.ts` to fix it is out of scope.
- **The e2e English check.** `englishProblems` in `e2e/support/playthrough.ts` needs a capital first letter. `capitalised(source)` covers "your hero" and "the opponent's hero".
- **Translation lookups.** The new keys are longer than the existing ones, so they are tried first when the engine's sentences are matched. Each needs ", aiming at" or "dealt", so no existing sentence matches them.

## Open questions

None block the build. These are the decisions this plan made, with the alternative rejected for each:

- **Units in the new lines** are named as every other log line names them, with no "your" or "the opponent's". Rejected: an owner prefix, because the owner is unknown once the unit has left the board.
- **Several targets** are joined with `listSeparator()` (`"; "`, or `"；"` for a Chinese reader), the log's existing list idiom. Rejected: `Intl.ListFormat`.
- **Targets the view hid, or that can't be named,** are dropped, and with none left the play line reads as today. Rejected: printing "a card".
- **A whole-Armor hit with a source** reads "…Armor absorbed N damage from {source}", because R1361 says nothing was dealt. Rejected: "{source} dealt 0 damage".
````

## Risks

- **Hidden information (R97, CLAUDE.md rule 7).** Names come only from `name.known`. That reads only the board's public zones, the viewer's own hand and the window's public events, so it is null for `"hidden"`. A face-down announce is never stored.
- **Pairing by object.** `aims` is keyed by the event object. `keptLineFor(view)` and the window lines both pass objects taken from that same `view.events` (`newEventsSince` slices, it does not copy). A test that reuses one `cardPlayed` object twice in a window would pair both with the last announce, which is why test 5b spreads the second one.
- **Line flip in the window.** A window line is redrawn from the current view (R745). For a view or two, the announce can slide out before its `cardPlayed` does, and the line then reads plainly until it moves to history, which keeps its arrival-time text. The issue accepts this fallback. Changing `useLogHistory.ts` to fix it is out of scope.
- **The e2e English check.** `englishProblems` in `e2e/support/playthrough.ts` needs a capital first letter. `capitalised(source)` covers "your hero" and "the opponent's hero".
- **Translation lookups.** The new keys are longer than the existing ones, so they are tried first when the engine's sentences are matched. Each needs ", aiming at" or "dealt", so no existing sentence matches them.

## Goal

The game log uses two facts the engine already sends.

- **Play lines.** A `cardPlayed` reads "{seat} played {card} for {cost}, aiming at {targets}" when the `cardAnnounced` of the same instance, earlier in the same window, declared targets the viewer can name.
- **Damage lines.** A non-combat `damage` whose `sourceId` the viewer can name reads "{source} dealt {amount} damage to {target}", with an Armor form. A `damageAbsorbed` with such a source reads "{target}'s Armor absorbed {absorbed} damage from {source}".

  - combat hits;
  - a source that is hidden, null or can't be named;
  - a face-down set;
  - a play whose targets can't be read, or that has none;
  - a play whose announce has left the window;
  - a countered play.
- **Translation.** Each new sentence is one whole `t()` key with a zh-CN entry (R711000).

   ```ts
   /** Each `cardPlayed` in a window → the targets its announce declared (B5 E1): see `announcedAims`. */
   type Aims = ReadonlyMap<GameEvent, readonly string[]>;

   /**
    * Each play in the window → what its `cardAnnounced` declared: the latest announce of the same instance
    * before it, keyed by the `cardPlayed` event itself so a card played twice in one window pairs each play
    * with its own. A face-down set (the other seat reads its targets as the sentinel, and its play takes a
    * fresh id, R97, R227) and a hidden announce pair with nothing, nor does a play whose announce has left
    * the window: each reads as it always did.
    */
   function announcedAims(events: readonly GameEvent[]): Aims {
     const declared = new Map<string, readonly string[]>();
     const aims = new Map<GameEvent, readonly string[]>();
     for (const event of events) {
       if (event.type === "cardAnnounced") {
         if (event.instanceId !== HIDDEN_CARD && event.faceDown !== true) declared.set(event.instanceId, event.targets);
       } else if (event.type === "cardPlayed") {
         const targets = declared.get(event.instanceId);
         if (targets !== undefined) aims.set(event, targets);
         declared.delete(event.instanceId);
       }
     }
     return aims;
   }
   ```

   | damage `e1`→`u1`, 1, `absorbed: 2` | `${V} dealt 1 damage to ${P}, 2 absorbed by Armor` |
   | damage `hero-p2`→`hero-p1`, 2 | `The opponent's hero dealt 2 damage to your hero` |
   | damageAbsorbed `e1`→`u1`, 3 | `${P}'s Armor absorbed 3 damage from ${V}` |
   | damageAbsorbed `e1`→`u1`, 3, combat | `${P}'s Armor absorbed 3 damage in combat` |
   | damageAbsorbed `"hidden"`→`u1`, 3 | `${P}'s Armor absorbed 3 damage` |

   - `P` is `nameOf(PANTHER)` and `V` is `nameOf(VANILLA)`.
   - Every event not marked combat has `combat: false`.

5. **`it("R745 keeps a play's aim once it leaves the window, pairs each play with its own announce, and reads as before when its announce is out of reach", …)`**
   - **(a) The aim survives into history.**
     - Let `filler` be 32 events of the form `{ type: "healthLost", player: "p1", amount: i + 1 }`, and `turn` be `[announce(["u1"]), PLAY, HIT]`.
     - Build three views: `withEvents(board(), turn)`, then `withEvents(board(), [...turn, ...filler.slice(0, 29)])`, then `withEvents(board(), filler)`.
     - Fold them with `views.reduce((h, view) => advanceLogHistory(h, view, keptLineFor(view, lookup)), EMPTY_LOG_HISTORY)`.
     - Expect `history.seats.p1?.kept.map((line) => line.text)` to equal `[AIMED, DEALT]`.
   - **(b) Each play pairs with its own announce.**
     - Events: `[announce(["u1"]), PLAY, announce(["hero-p1"]), { ...PLAY }]`. The second play must be a distinct object.
     - Expect: `[AIMED, \`Opponent played ${nameOf(SPELL)} for 1, aiming at your hero\`]`.
   - **(c) Fallback when the announce is out of reach.**
     - Render `withEvents(board(), [PLAY, HIT])`.
     - Expect: `[\`Opponent played ${nameOf(SPELL)} for 1\`, DEALT]`.

- [ ] A spell played at an enemy unit logs one play line naming that unit (test 1).
- [ ] Its damage logs "{source} dealt N damage to {target}", and combat lines are unchanged (tests 1 and 4).
- [ ] A face-down set, and any target or source the view hid, logs exactly what it logs today (tests 3 and 4).
- [ ] A play with no targets logs today's line (tests 3 and 5c).
- [ ] The aim survives the window into history (test 5a).
- [ ] The four zh-CN entries are added, and `i18n.test.ts` (R711000) passes.

## Risks

- **Hidden information (R97, CLAUDE.md rule 7).** Names come only from `name.known`. That reads only the board's public zones, the viewer's own hand and the window's public events, so it is null for `"hidden"`. A face-down announce is never stored.
- **Pairing by object.** `aims` is keyed by the event object. `keptLineFor(view)` and the window lines both pass objects taken from that same `view.events` (`newEventsSince` slices, it does not copy). A test that reuses one `cardPlayed` object twice in a window would pair both with the last announce, which is why test 5b spreads the second one.
- **Line flip in the window.** A window line is redrawn from the current view (R745). For a view or two, the announce can slide out before its `cardPlayed` does, and the line then reads plainly until it moves to history, which keeps its arrival-time text. The issue accepts this fallback. Changing `useLogHistory.ts` to fix it is out of scope.
- **The e2e English check.** `englishProblems` in `e2e/support/playthrough.ts` needs a capital first letter. `capitalised(source)` covers "your hero" and "the opponent's hero".
- **Translation lookups.** The new keys are longer than the existing ones, so they are tried first when the engine's sentences are matched. Each needs ", aiming at" or "dealt", so no existing sentence matches them.

## Open questions

None block the build. These are the decisions this plan made, with the alternative rejected for each:

- **Units in the new lines** are named as every other log line names them, with no "your" or "the opponent's". Rejected: an owner prefix, because the owner is unknown once the unit has left the board.
- **Several targets** are joined with `listSeparator()` (`"; "`, or `"；"` for a Chinese reader), the log's existing list idiom. Rejected: `Intl.ListFormat`.
- **Targets the view hid, or that can't be named,** are dropped, and with none left the play line reads as today. Rejected: printing "a card".
- **A whole-Armor hit with a source** reads "…Armor absorbed N damage from {source}", because R1361 says nothing was dealt. Rejected: "{source} dealt 0 damage".
